correctness.rationale: Recomputed common-increment Euler and stochastic-Heun updates: their difference equals -(lambda^2 h^2/2)x+(lambda g h^(3/2)/2)Z. Scaling gives noncentral chi-square df=d with Delta=lambda^2 h ||x||^2/g^2. Monotone inverse-power mapping yields exact raw survival and cap atoms. Noncentral chi-square gamma/Poisson mixture has nonzero small-ball density constant, yielding regular-variation exponent d/k and sharp moment cutoff. Central chi-square Cramer theorem gives both dimension-rate limits. check_distribution.py empirically verifies laws and finite-d thresholds. No finite computation substitutes for the analytic proof. All quantified boundaries include d>=1, h/lambda/g/T>0 and k>0; clipping bounds m,M finite.

value.rationale: The stochastic noise-normalized PI step controller has a natural, operationally important exact invariant: probability of hitting either hard step multiplier cap. The theorem classifies this for all states, dimensions, step sizes and nonnegative PI gains in an OU benchmark, additionally locating the exact moment integrability boundary of the raw proposal and giving sharp high-dimensional exponential cap-frequency laws. Those concrete thresholds quantify why clipping changes the probabilistic behavior, and supply a directly reproducible test for stochastic adaptive-step implementations. No general sampler convergence/quality theorem is claimed; the fact is still a motivated complete classification, not a chosen numerical slice or textbook identity alone.
